title: I made 20 free little browser games, which one would you actually play twice?
author: juanludlf
selftext:
I've been making small games in my spare time and putting them all on one site. They're free, run in the browser (phones too), and you don't need to download anything or sign up.

I didn't want to just clone the classics, so each one has a twist:

- **Tic-tac-toe, backwards:** make three in a row and you lose. The goblin goes first, and a draw isn't enough.
- **The maze:** get across it in the dark before your lantern goes out. Some portals are shortcuts, some are traps.
- **Liar's Dice** against One-eyed Borgan. Raise the bid or call his bluff.
- **The cup sharp:** three cups, one ball and a dealer who looks far too calm.
- **Lines 98:** the old ball-lines game, except Windows 98 pop-ups keep getting in your way.
- **The porter:** a tightrope walk where birds land on your pole.
- **The Treasures of Erandel:** everyone digs on the same huge island, looking for one pirate chest.

There's also pairs, archery, seven and a half, a tavern drum concert and Triara, a fantasy team manager.

You start with 1,000 free coins. If you save up 100,000, you take the throne on the homepage and can write whatever you want there until someone knocks you off.

So far the maze is the most played, but honestly most of those plays are mine. So I'd love an honest answer:

**Which one is your favourite, and which one did you close after 10 seconds?**

https://erandel.com
